Article Title: 'To clean-shaven face & head': Owaisi's 'moustache' challenge to Yogi, Akhilesh over CM fight in UP
Article Text:
​Owaisi takes a swipe at Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav, backing Chandrashekhar Azad as the Samajik Parivartan Morcha’s CM face for the 2027 UP polls

NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Thursday took a swipe at Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav , saying neither would become the chief minister after the 2027 assembly elections.Addressing the Samajik Parivartan Morcha's first joint rally in Lucknow, he said the next chief minister would be someone with a moustache, in an apparent reference to alliance partner Chandrashekhar Azad."Someone remarked that this is an alliance between the bearded and the moustachioed. And, in truth, it is. Now, I wish to address that clean-shaven face and the other clean-shaved head, you will not become the CM anymore; it will be someone with a moustache..," he said.Owaisi accused the BJP and the Samajwadi Party of failing to protect the Constitution and ensure adequate political representation for Muslims.Invoking Dr BR Ambedkar, he said the Constitution guaranteed liberty, fraternity, justice and equality. He accused the RSS and the Sangh Parivar of working against these principles."Justice will not come through bulldozers or encounters. Justice will come through Babasaheb Ambedkar's Constitution.The rule of law will be restored," he said, targeting the BJP government.He also criticised the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that it was being used to weaken the Constitution.Targeting the Samajwadi Party, Owaisi accused its leadership of practising caste-based politics and seeking Muslim votes without ensuring adequate representation to the community."How many times will we be betrayed? Akhilesh Yadav, will you give a ticket to a Muslim from Karhal?" he asked. Yadav had won the Karhal seat in the 2022 Assembly elections.Owaisi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adityanath of promoting communal divisions while failing to address unemployment and concerns over education.He said the Morcha, if voted to power, would focus on education and employment for young people."We will ensure education for young people and jobs after they complete their education. We will make doctors and engineers, and ensure that our students get opportunity to study in IITs," he said.Referring to the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, Owaisi urged people to support the Morcha's candidates in the 2027 elections."The historic opportunity before us is that we should support neither the red cap (of Samajwadi Party) nor the RSS-BJP," he said.Praising Azad, Owaisi said he could represent the poor, oppressed and deprived sections of society."If there can be a chief minister in Uttar Pradesh who represents the poor, the oppressed and the deprived, and whose government will be of the people rather than only a particular section, his name will be Chandrashekhar Azad," he said."I am confident that with our unity, prayers and hard work, we will make Chandrashekhar Azad the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh. Together, we will prevent the BJP from forming the government for a third time," Owaisi said.
Article Summary: Owaisi backs Chandrashekhar Azad as the Samajik Parivartan Morcha’s CM face for the 2027 UP polls. Owaisi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adityanath of promoting communal divisions while failing to address unemployment and concerns over education.

Article Title: ‘Modi is sitting quietly today’: Kharge hints at BJP top brass rift, jibes at Yogi over PM ambitions
Article Text:
Kharge spoke at 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Lucknow

Kharge questions BJP's Rs 10,000 crore funds

Congress holds Constitution Day march in Lucknow

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday credited the people of Uttar Pradesh with checking the BJP 's electoral ambitions in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying their verdict had forced Prime Minister Narendra Modi to go quiet on his '400 paar' slogan.Addressing a 'Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan' at the Congress office in Lucknow on Constitution Day , Kharge also accused the BJP of allowing its funds to swell while inflation, unemployment and the prices of cooking gas and essential food items continued to rise."I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, 'Abki Baar, 400 Paar' (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today," Kharge said.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won 36 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections.Kharge also claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah had reduced his public statements, adding, "I do not know whether the two (Modi and Shah) are getting along or not."In a veiled reference to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, the Congress chief said another leader in Lucknow also had his eyes on the prime minister's chair.Targeting the BJP over its finances, Kharge questioned the source of nearly Rs 10,000 crore in party funds, alleging that the ruling party was benefiting from the use of central investigative agencies to intimidate people and collect money."Everything has become expensive. But the BJP's coffers are filling up. Where has the BJP got Rs 10,000 crore in its party funds from? You question us, but we want to ask you where this Rs 10,000 crore came from," he said.The BJP has cash and deposits worth nearly Rs 10,000 crore, according to its annual audit report recently submitted to the Election Commission.Kharge alleged that the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Income Tax Department and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were being used to threaten people and extract money."By deploying the ED, Income Tax Department and CBI to threaten people and extract money, the BJP is filling its coffers. This is nothing short of robbery," he said.The Congress organised a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Lucknow on Thursday to mark Constitution Day. However, the march did not reach its intended destination, with Kharge alleging that the state government was afraid of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.Kharge said the government had begun fearing even the party's shadows and asserted that Congress workers would take out the march whenever an opportunity arose.Kharge also recalled the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, and highlighted Uttar Pradesh's contribution to the process. He referred to a resolution passed by the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly in October 1937 calling for the repeal of the Government of India Act, 1935, and the framing of India's Constitution by an elected Constituent Assembly.Earlier, Kharge paid tribute to the ashes of BR Ambedkar at the Ambedkar Mahasabha in Lucknow before heading to the Congress office. Congress state president Aradhana Misra Mona, MP Imran Masood and the party's state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam were among those present.Meanwhile, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused the Modi government of undermining parliamentary democracy and disregarding parliamentary conventions. Addressing reporters during the march, he said the party was holding protests at state headquarters across the country over concerns about Parliament's functioning and the protection of the Constitution."They have turned Parliament into a complete mockery; even after 106 days, they haven't even prorogued Parliament," Venugopal said, questioning the delay in convening the Winter Session.He also alleged that the government had denied people an opportunity to observe Constitution Day through parliamentary proceedings, and asked why there was no indication of when the Winter Session would begin.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge credits people of Uttar Pradesh with checking BJP's electoral ambitions in 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Kharge also accused the BJP of allowing its funds to swell while inflation, unemployment and the prices of cooking gas and essential food items continued to rise. Congress organised a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Lucknow on Thursday to mark Constitution Day.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday released his party's "PDA manifesto" ahead of the UP assembly polls. The announcement comes on Constitution Day The PDA, a political formulation promoted by Akhilesh Yadav, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities). The SP has indicated that releasing its manifesto months before the polls will allow it to take its proposals to the public ahead of the election campaign.The party is expected to announce two more detailed manifesto, including a district-level framework.In the party's election manifesto release, Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the rival BJP, saying: "When a few dominant, supremacists and selfish people want to keep their thousands of years of power intact and in that attempt want to not only amend and change but also erase the Constitution - all of us those who love the Constitution should take it up as our national and social duty to unite and thwart all conspiracies to amend the Constitution".He further said: "Our country will be governed by 'Samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'Manvidhan' (arbitrariness). There are a few powers who want to do this through 'Manvidhan' and not 'Samvidhan'. There is an ongoing war over Constitution. On one hand, there are those who want to misue the Constitution to come to power. One the other hand is PDA, who wants the rule of social justice of the Constitution, we want to erase all differences, uphold reservation and equality..."Akhilesh Yadav's annoucement comes as relations between Congress and his party appeared to sour after the SP jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming polls.The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties. To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.Later, SP offered 26 seats to the Congress, which triggered unease on the second day of the seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls between the two alliance partners in Delhi on Tuesday.According to reports, SP’s offer of 26 seats came after the Congress tabled a list of 120 seats of its choice.Unease was noticeable in the Congress camp over SP’s 26-seat offer as Saharanpur MP and member of Congress’s negotiating team Imran Masood objected to media claims of SP’s 36-seat offer.The SP is expected to contest the 2027 assembly elections in alliance with the Congress against the BJP-led govt in UP. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, while the SP governed under Akhilesh from 2012 to 2017. The Bahujan Samaj Party(BSP), led by Mayawati, was in power from 2007 to 2012.The 403-member UP assembly is expected to witness a major contest between the BJP and the SP-led opposition, with alliances and the mobilisation of different social groups likely to play an important role in the campaign. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while its ally Apna Dal (Sonelal) secured 12.The SP won 111 seats, while its allies also won seats. The Congress secured two seats, and the BSP one. The SP received approximately 32% of the vote in the 2022 polls, emerging as the principal opposition party in the state.By choosing to release its manifesto on the Constitution Day, the SP has linked the launch of its electoral programme to a day associated with constitutional values and democratic institutions.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav releases his party's "PDA manifesto" ahead of the UP assembly polls. The announcement comes on Constitution Day. The SP is expected to contest the 2027 assembly elections in alliance with the Congress against the BJP-led govt in UP.

Reels could amount to unauthorised business

Prior approval required for railway-related content

NEW DELHI: The North Central Railway (NCR) has warned its employees against making and posting social media reels during duty hours, saying the activity distracts staff and jeopardises train operations.In an advisory issued on November 17, 2027, the railway zone cautioned that employees could face disciplinary action for violating safety protocols or engaging in unauthorised commercial activities through content creation.The communication was addressed to senior officials of its three divisions, Prayagraj, Jhansi and Agra, and its workshops. The zone said some railway employees were creating and posting reels on their social media accounts while on duty, which could compromise operational safety."Performing such activities during duty hours poses a severe distraction, jeopardises safety in train operations, and compromises administrative integrity," the NCR zone said as quoted by PTI.The railway zone also flagged the possibility of employees earning money through social media content, saying this could amount to running an unauthorised commercial enterprise or side business."Moreover, there is a strong likelihood that some staff are deriving monetary advantage through their (social media) content creation, which amounts to running an unauthorised commercial enterprise/side business, which is a direct violation of Rule 15 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966," it said.The zone warned that filming on railway premises or equipment for commercial purposes without formal permission or payment of prescribed fees was prohibited."Filming on Railway premises or equipment for commercial gain without formal permission or without payment of prescribed film shooting/commercial fees is prohibited."It added that if social media posts were found to be generating commercial benefits, the prescribed fees would have to be paid. Failure to do so could invite penal action.The NCR zone also clarified that employees creating educational or awareness-related content about the Railways would need prior approval from the competent authority."Posts intended for educational or socio-awareness generation regarding Railways may only be published with the prior approval of the Competent Authority," it said.It further directed employees who frequently post content on social media to submit a formal undertaking to the railway administration."Staff who frequently post content on social media must submit a formal undertaking to the Railway Administration confirming that they derive no monetary advantage from such posts and that their activities do not compromise Railway safety or security."Divisional and workshop authorities have been directed to closely monitor the active social media accounts of railway personnel. The zone warned that employees found violating safety protocols or engaging in social media activities during duty hours would face strict disciplinary action.
Article Summary: The North Central Railway (NCR) has warned its employees against making and posting social media reels during duty hours. The zone said some railway employees were creating and posting reels on their social media accounts while on duty, which could compromise operational safety. The railway zone also flagged the possibility of employees earning money through social media content.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule on Thursday dismissed speculation about her party joining the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and claims that Sharad Pawar was seeking the Maharashtra chief minister's post for her, saying she was elected to serve the people of Baramati and not "indulge in political gossip"."I am a serious politician and a serious policymaker. I do not waste my time on gossip. The people of the Baramati Lok Sabha constituency sent me to Delhi not to indulge in gossip. They sent me there to work and serve the state and the country," she told news agency PTResponding to questions about the speculation surrounding her political future, Sule urged journalists to focus on policy, accountability and governance rather than unsubstantiated reports.On claims that Sharad Pawar, who is admitted in Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital with suspected dehydration, wanted her to become chief minister, she recalled that her late cousin Ajit Pawar had consistently maintained over the past 40 years that anyone commanding the required numbers in the state legislature could occupy the post.She also asked journalists to question her about her parliamentary work, including her contributions to four Joint Parliamentary Committees (JPCs) and the Finance Committee."Ask me what I have achieved through the four JPCs I have served on. I am on the Finance Committee. What is my position on the issues before it? What impact will US President Donald Trump's tariffs have on people's daily lives? These are the questions that matter," she said.On reports of internal differences within the NCP (SP), Sule said everyone in a democracy had the right to express their views while also being willing to listen."In a strong democracy, everyone has the right to express their views. Just as I have the strength to speak, I must also have the strength to listen," she said.She maintained that Sharad Pawar, who founded the NCP, continued to be its president and alleged that injustice had been done to him in the dispute over the party's name and election symbol."We submitted all documents and evidence before the Election Commission, but injustice was still done to Pawar saheb. Our fight for the party continued yesterday, continues today and will continue tomorrow," she said."Until Sharad Pawar gets justice and regains the party that he founded, our fight will continue," she added.On Maharashtra's law and order situation, Sule said she had urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the Home portfolio, to take the matter seriously.Citing Union home ministry data, she said Pune had the highest crime figures in Maharashtra and expressed concern over the city's reputation as a safe educational hub."I have no personal issue with the Pune Police Commissioner. The accountability must be fixed on the administration and the system overseeing the police," she said.While expressing confidence in Maharashtra Police personnel, she called for accountability within the administration overseeing the force."We are not interested in allegations and counter-allegations. Public safety is important, and we must discuss the issue and find a solution," she said.Sule added that the NCP (SP), which represents two Lok Sabha constituencies in Pune district through her and Amol Kolhe, would cooperate with the government on public safety.On the party's organisational activities, she said all NCP (SP) MPs had submitted details about the implementation of the VB-G RAM G scheme and the disbursement of funds to farmers following requests from Sharad Pawar and Maharashtra unit chief Shashikant Shinde.The party plans to discuss the information with its office-bearers at the district, taluka and village levels over the next one-and-a-half to two months.Sule also said the party would work constructively with the government on farmers' issues and development rather than oppose it merely for the sake of opposition.On Constitution Day, she stressed that laws must apply equally to political parties and private companies."If companies such as Colgate or Godrej put up advertisements or hoardings, they have to pay the required charges. Political parties should also be subject to the same rules. Those in power must practise what they preach," she said.Recalling the November 26, 2008, Mumbai terror attacks, Sule said she had lost three to four friends in the incident."I remember that day as if it happened yesterday," she said, recalling how she had rushed out with family members and friends after hearing about the attacks. Their vehicle was stopped near Wilson College, and they initially thought it was an accident or a smaller emergency."It was a huge personal loss for all of us," she said.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule dismissed speculation about her party joining the BJP- led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Sule said she was elected to serve the people of Baramati and not "indulge in political gossip"

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday finally broke silence on Imran Masood's aggressive attack on Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh.Speaking at an event in Lucknow, Kharge advised Masood to "focus on action rather than just words", as the Saharanpur MP's increasingly sharp remarks against ally Samajwadi Party (SP) have added to the strain over seat-sharing negotiations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."... Imran Masood — whom I frequently hear on television, where he often speaks with great passion. However, we must focus on action rather than just words; the more we work together, the further we will progress. He is in Parliament, where he consistently fights for the party and strives to ensure that our positions are upheld," Kharge said.The Congress chief's remarks come amid growing friction between the two INDIA bloc allies, with Masood repeatedly questioning the SP's approach to seat-sharing even as discussions between the parties remain under way.Masood on Thursday questioned the rationale behind continuing seat-sharing discussions after the Akhilesh Yadav-led SP announced five candidates while negotiations with the Congress were still in progress."It is no alliance if one partner 'leaves' seats for the other after announcing its candidates," he said, raising questions about whether the Congress was being treated as an equal partner.The Congress MP also made it clear that he would remain with his party and would not accept a subordinate position in the alliance."What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us? We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.Masood, who was involved in the seat-sharing discussions, argued that an alliance should involve joint decisions and announcements. He declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, which was scheduled to be released later on Thursday, saying he was unaware of the party's approach."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.Recalling the previous Assembly elections contested by the Congress and SP, Masood said his party had fought 107 seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh."Now, he is yet to become the chief minister," he added.Masood's latest remarks follow a series of public attacks on the SP leadership over the alliance arrangement. On Wednesday, he had used sharp expressions to convey his frustration with what he described as the SP's treatment of the Congress.In an interview with The Times of India, he questioned whether the SP wanted to fight the BJP or its own alliance partner.(I am unable to understand your battle … You want to fight the BJP or us. If you will want to stand on my neck and build a Taj Mahal on my grave, I will be suffocated. I will fight back)," he had said.Later, speaking to a television channel, Masood compared the Congress to zero, arguing that its presence multiplied the strength of an alliance partner by ten."If you don't understand our importance, then OK, Goodbye, Thank You," he said.The SP had largely refrained from responding to his remarks throughout Wednesday. However, his repeated criticism prompted some SP functionaries to question the Congress leadership's silence.A senior SP functionary told TOI that either the Congress leadership was choosing to ignore the statements or was unaware of what its leaders were saying. Neither possibility, he suggested, was a positive sign for the alliance.The functionary also pointed out that Masood and AICC's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had previously targeted the SP leadership over the alliance, but SP leaders had avoided responding following instructions from party chief Akhilesh Yadav not to comment publicly on seat-sharing discussions.The SP's concern, according to the functionary, was not merely that Congress leaders were criticising the party, but that the Congress leadership had not publicly objected to what it considered unprovoked remarks.
Article Summary: Kharge advises Masood to "focus on action rather than just words" Masood questions SP's approach to seat-sharing negotiations. Earlier barbs had put SP on the defensive. Masood says he will not accept a subordinate position in the alliance.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday refused to interfere with a trial court's decision to frame criminal charges against Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav , his wife Rabri Devi and son Tejashwi Yadav in the alleged IRCTC hotel scam case.A single-judge bench of Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma dismissed the petitions filed by the three RJD leaders, thereby upholding the trial court's October 13, 2025, order directing that charges be framed against them.The order had been passed by Special Judge (PC Act) Vishal Gogne of the Rouse Avenue Courts, who had directed that the accused face charges related to corruption, criminal conspiracy and cheating.Lalu Prasad Yadav, Rabri Devi and Tejashwi Yadav had approached the high court separately, questioning the legality of the trial court's decision. They argued that the prosecution had not presented sufficient material to establish a prima facie case against them.Rabri Devi maintained that the trial court had wrongly framed charges against her based on presumptions, without properly examining the evidence available on record.Tejashwi Yadav, too, argued that there was insufficient material to justify proceeding against him.The high court had earlier issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on the criminal revision petitions filed by the family members.They had also sought a stay on the proceedings before the trial court.During an earlier hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Lalu Prasad Yadav, had argued that the CBI filed its charge sheet before obtaining the required sanction for prosecution.He also submitted that the transactions in question were carried out in accordance with government policy and, therefore, could not be treated as offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.The case concerns alleged irregularities in the leasing of two IRCTC hotels between 2004 and 2009, when Lalu Prasad Yadav was the Union railway minister.According to the CBI, the hotels were leased out in violation of prescribed procedures during his tenure. One of the properties was allotted to Sarla Gupta, the wife of Prem Gupta, a close associate of Lalu Prasad Yadav and a Rajya Sabha MP at the time.The investigating agency has alleged that the hotel deals were linked to the transfer of around three acres of prime land to a company associated with the Yadav family through a benami arrangement.The CBI has alleged that the land transfer was part of a quid pro quo arrangement connected to the hotel allotments.
Article Summary: A single-judge bench dismissed the petitions filed by the three RJD leaders. Lalu Prasad Yadav, Rabri Devi and Tejashwi Yadav had approached the high court separately. The case concerns alleged irregularities in the leasing of two IRCTC hotels.

Article Title: 'Zero tolerance for terrorism': EAM Jaishankar remembers 26/11 victims on attack anniversary
Article Text:
EAM pays tribute to 26/11 terror attack victims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent lives lost and the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice while fighting the terrorists.Marking 18 years since the attacks that shook the country, Jaishankar reiterated India's commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and bringing those responsible to justice."Remember innocent lives lost & salute the brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. Committed to combating terrorism in all its forms & manifestations and bringing those involved to justice. Zero tolerance for terrorism," Jaishankar wrote in a post on X.This year marks 18 years since 10 Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists launched a series of coordinated attacks across Mumbai, targeting some of the city's busiest locations.Commonly known as 26/11, the attacks began on the night of November 26, 2008, when the terrorists entered Mumbai by sea. Over the next four days, they carried out strikes at several locations, killing 166 people and injuring around 300.Among the targets were the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi-Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. Several of these locations were frequented by foreign nationals and Mumbai's workforce.The attacks left a lasting impact on the city, with the memories of the siege continuing to haunt survivors and families of those killed. Bullet marks at Leopold Cafe and Nariman House, along with memorials honouring the security personnel who lost their lives, remain reminders of the tragedy.Nine of the 10 terrorists were killed during the security operation, while the lone surviving attacker, Pakistani national Mohammad Ajmal Amir Kasab, was captured. Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble played a crucial role in apprehending Kasab before succumbing to his injuries.Kasab was sentenced to death in May 2010 and hanged at Yerawada Central Prison in Pune on November 21, 2012.
Article Summary: This year marks 18 years since 10 Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists launched a series of coordinated attacks across Mumbai. The attacks began on the night of November 26, 2008, when the terrorists entered Mumbai by sea. Over the next four days, they carried out strikes at several locations, killing 166 people and injuring around 300.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying it would be premature to oppose the legislation before its details are known.Her comments come amid broader opposition resistance to the NDA government's push for delimitation."Let the bill come. Article Title: ‘Meta BJP ka Beta’: Zuckerberg posters in RSS attire emerge in Bengaluru as Youth Congress protests
Article Text:
Youth Congress targets Zuckerberg with RSS-themed posters in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: Mark Zuckerberg has got a political makeover in Bengaluru, with the Karnataka Pradesh Youth Congress putting up posters depicting the Meta chief executive in Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) attire and branding him “Mark BJP berg”. The satirical posters of Zuckerberg come as the Youth Congress accuse the social media giant of favouring the ruling BJP.The campaign, led by Karnataka Pradesh Youth Congress Committee president H S Manjunath Gowda, features the slogan “Meta BJP ka Beta” and has appeared at several locations across the city, including Sadahalli Gate on New Airport Road, near the toll plaza and in Chikkajala.The Youth Congress shared photographs of the posters on X, saying: “BJP ka Beta Meta enters to Namma Bengaluru! Mark Bjpberg is getting famous than Meta.”The campaign is part of a wider confrontation between the Congress and Meta over allegations that the company selectively restricts opposition voices while failing to act impartially on fake news, hate speech and user privacy.The party has accused Meta of applying its content moderation policies unevenly across political groups and questioned whether its platforms are being used in ways that undermine democratic values.Meta has maintained that it follows Indian law and remains politically neutral.The poster campaign follows protests by Indian Youth Congress workers at Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram over alleged restrictions on the social media accounts of Congress leaders and other opposition figures.In a post dated November 21, the Youth Congress alleged that Meta had withheld the Instagram accounts of Indian Youth Congress president and a national in-charge at the BJP’s behest. It claimed the accounts were restored within 15 minutes of protests outside the company’s offices, and questioned whether the timing was a “coincidence”.The organisation issued a seven-day ultimatum to Meta, demanding that it remove restrictions on accounts belonging to opposition leaders, journalists and content creators.“Must Indians visit your offices every time you silence them?” it asked.The protests have since spread to several cities, including Delhi, Kolkata, Patna and Bengaluru, with demonstrators demanding that Meta explain how its algorithms decide which political posts are restricted and restore accounts taken down on government orders.Amid the escalating row, Meta officials met Congress leaders at the party headquarters in New Delhi on Tuesday. Meta executives Aman Jain and Natasha Jog met AICC social media department chairperson Supriya Shrinate, following a request from the company.Congress leaders raised concerns over what they described as growing restrictions on opposition accounts and posts, alleging that Meta was interfering in Indian politics and favouring the BJP.Meta officials said the company was bound by Indian laws and had to remove posts within three hours of a government request. They reiterated that the company was politically neutral and made no commitments to the Congress, people familiar with the discussions said.The meeting also came after Meta executives expressed concern over protests targeting the company’s offices and posters featuring Zuckerberg in RSS attire.The dispute has drawn attention to the scale of content restrictions imposed by Meta in India. The company restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts under local laws in the first half of 2026, compared with around 70,000 during the whole of 2025, according to company disclosures cited by Reuters.Meta has attributed the increase to amendments to India’s information technology rules, which require platforms to remove content more quickly and proactively. The rising number of restrictions has renewed concerns over freedom of expression as the government steps up requests for online content removal.
Article Summary: Youth Congress targets Zuckerberg with RSS-themed posters in Bengaluru. The satirical posters of Zuckerberg come as the Youth Congress accuse the social media giant of favouring the ruling BJP. The poster campaign follows protests by Indian Youth Congress workers at Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram.

Article Title: India tops in videos removed from YouTube
Article Text:
YouTube was also the most targeted Google service in a separate dataset tracking removal requests from Indian courts and govt agencies. accounting for 3,399 of the 4,006 requests Google received from India between Jan and June

India’s removal requests to Google jump 61% in 6 months

NEW DELHI: YouTube removed 34.4 lakh videos uploaded from India between April and June 2026, the most from any country. The figure rose 28% from the previous quarter and accounted for nearly 31% of the 1.1 crore videos YouTube took down worldwide under its Community Guidelines.The US was second at 12.4 lakh, followed by Indonesia at 9.2 lakh.Child safety accounted for 68.2% of video removals globally, and automated systems first flagged 98.6% of the videos taken down.YouTube identifies the country of upload using the uploader’s IP address and publishes the reasons for removal only at the global level.YouTube was also the most targeted Google service in a separate dataset tracking removal requests from Indian courts and govt agencies. It accounted for 3,399 of the 4,006 requests Google received from India between Jan and June, according to Google’s Transparency Report.Across Google services, requests from India rose 61% from the preceding six months and covered 65,091 items. Only Russia and South Korea sent more requests. Police accounted for 2,870 requests, or nearly 72% of India’s total, while courts accounted for 695. Defamation was the most frequently cited reason, appearing in 2,130 requests. In response to Indian requests, Google removed 19,883 items for violating local laws and another 1,415 under its own policies. It took no action on 19,402 items and said it lacked sufficient information to act on another 17,473.
Article Summary: The US was second at 12.4 lakh, followed by Indonesia at 9.2 lakh. Child safety accounted for 68.2% of video removals globally. Across Google services, requests from India rose 61% from the preceding six months and covered 65,091 items.

Article Title: Mumbai sees highest post-monsoon python rescues in 5 years as unseasonal rain, temperature swings and habitat loss push 19 Indian rock pythons into residential areas, highways and parking lots across
Article Text:
On Octo 5th, an eight-foot-long Indian rock python is safely rescued from an iron light pole at Kalanagar in Bandra East

Key Highlights

Indian rock pythons rescued across MMR since October, the highest post-monsoon rescue count in five years.

Mumbai accounted for 11 rescues, while Navi Mumbai and Thane reported four each.

RAWW received at least 48 distress calls and sighting reports in just one week, though several snakes escaped before they could be rescued.

Unseasonal October rain and sharp temperature fluctuations may have disrupted winter dormancy, triggering increased movement, mating activity or hunting.

Habitat loss , mangrove destruction and construction projects across areas such as BKC and Mulund may be pushing pythons into residential spaces and drainage networks.





MUMBAI: Around midday last Tuesday, an Indian rock python (Python molurus) was spotted hightailing into a Pali Village grotto in Bandra. It wasn’t the only constrictor spotted in the city.Since Oct, Resqink Association for Wildlife Welfare (RAWW) has rescued 19 Indian rock pythons across MMR—11 in Mumbai and four each in Navi Mumbai and Thane—the most post-monsoon rescues of the species in the past five years. “These are only the rescue figures. We received at least 48 distress calls and sightings last week alone. Often, the snake escapes,” says RAWW founder Pawan Sharma. The organisation has rescued more than 233 Indian rock pythons in MMR since 2021.The snakes have turned up on bicycles, in parking lots and building corridors, and on Eastern Express Highway.Experts point to several causes. Sharma says unseasonal rains in late Oct and sharp temperature swings may have disrupted brumation, the winter dormancy of cold-blooded animals. Herpetologist Varad Giri agrees: “They’re more active during the monsoon and dormant in winter.” Unseasonal rain and warmth, he says, could signal that it’s time to mate, or trigger hormonal changes.The snakes may also be hunting.Habitat loss may be pushing them out too. Atul Kamble of Wildlife Animal Protection and Rescue Association suspects the destruction of urban forests and mangroves, and construction in once-wooded areas like BKC and Mulund. Metro operations and construction work across Mumbai have also made the underground the equivalent of a gaming arcade, especially for snakes that are highly sensitive to noise and vibration.Until a few years ago, stormwater and drainage systems were passable, if imperfect, resettlement colonies. But, Kamble says, the extensive loss of permeable spaces and the strain of a growing population have forced more runoff into the networks, causing them to flood and flush out the wildlife.He notes that people now tend to call experts rather than attack snakes, which suggests greater awareness. Or fear. Few know that the Indian rock python is a Schedule 1 animal, with the same legal protection as the tiger.Conservationists say data on how the species is responding to urbanisation is scarce. RAWW plans to propose a study to the state forest department.
Article Summary: Indian rock pythons rescued across MMR since October, the highest post-monsoon rescue count in five years. Mumbai accounted for 11 rescues, while Navi Mumbai and Thane reported four each. Unseasonal October rain and sharp temperature fluctuations may have disrupted winter dormancy, triggering increased movement.

Article Title: SC overturns Bihar govt's decision to free Anand Mohan in IAS officer murder case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday set aside the Bihar government's 2023 decision to grant remission to former MP Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case, giving him one month time to surrender and return to jail.Mohan was convicted in mob lynching and murder of then Gopalganj district magistrate G Krishnaiah. Article Title: 'We gave nine months to this case': 18 years after verdict, Ajmal Kasab's lawyers still await fees
Article Text:
Ajmal Kasab holding an AK-47.

Under legal provisions, courts appoint lawyers through legal services authorities when an accused is unable to engage counsel, ensuring that the person receives legal representation and a fair trial.

18 years since the Mumbai terror attacks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Eighteen years after the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, two lawyers who defended lone surviving terrorist Ajmal Kasab during his appeal are still waiting for their fees from the Maharashtra government.Advocates Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah represented Kasab before the Bombay high court for nine months after being appointed by the Maharashtra government in 2010. The two had set aside their other cases to defend the lone captured Pakistani terrorist, news agency PTI reported.They were nominated by the high court and appointed by the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) through a notification dated June 8, 2010, to represent Kasab in his appeal against the death sentence awarded by the trial court.According to the notification, signed by then secretary A K Sonawane, Solkar was to be paid on a par with a special public prosecutor, while Shah was entitled to remuneration equivalent to that of an additional public prosecutor handling a death penalty confirmation case.PTI citing official sources estimated the remuneration at Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,000 per day. However, both lawyers say their dues remain unpaid despite the high court proceedings having concluded more than a decade ago."We have still not received our fees for representing Kasab. I have been corresponding with the Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority time and again, but there seems to be no positive headway," Solkar told PTI.Solkar and Shah said that whenever they approached the MSLSA for payment, they were asked to submit detailed bills and memos specifying the dates and hours they appeared in court.They termed the demand unreasonable, arguing that it was difficult to maintain such detailed records of daily court hours after so many years.Solkar said their appointment letters clearly specified the remuneration payable, questioning why the government could not use the same pay scale to calculate and clear their dues."What is stopping the government from using the same pay scale and clearing our dues?" Solkar added.Shah also questioned the insistence on itemised bills when the government notification and the order passed by the then chief justice of the high court had clearly laid down their fee structure."We gave our entire day for nine months to argue this case. We had to keep all our other cases on the backburner so that there was no hurdle caused to the proceedings," Shah said.She added that the notification stipulated that their fees would be cleared after the high court delivered its verdict.An official from the state legal services authority, however, maintained that advocates are required to submit formal bills and memos for payment as per standard practice, the agency reported.In contrast, advocate Abbas Kazmi, who represented Kasab during the trial before special judge M L Tahaliyani, said his remuneration was cleared promptly. "My remuneration was cleared by the government soon after the completion of the trial," Kazmi said.The Bombay high court began hearing Kasab's death sentence confirmation case and his appeal in June 2010. It upheld the death sentence in February 2011. The Supreme Court subsequently affirmed the verdict.Kasab, who was lodged at Arthur Road prison after his capture was hanged at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune on November 21, 2012.Mumbai is marking the 18th anniversary of the November 26, 2008 terror attacks which killed 166 people, including foreign nationals, and left more than 300 injured.The attacks were carried out by 10 heavily armed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists who arrived in Mumbai by sea from Pakistan.The coordinated strikes targeted several prominent locations, including Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Trident Hotel, Nariman House (Chabad House), Leopold Cafe and Cama and Albless Hospital.The attacks began on the night of November 26 and continued until the morning of November 29, triggering a roughly 60-hour siege.The terrorists took hostages and engaged security personnel in prolonged gun battles, using the layout and height of buildings to their advantage.The operation was eventually brought to an end by Mumbai Police , armed police personnel, the Indian Navy's Marine Commandos and the National Security Guard (NSG).The attacks exposed significant gaps in coastal security, intelligence gathering and coordination among security agencies, prompting a major overhaul of India's counter-terrorism preparedness.Of the 10 attackers, Kasab was captured alive and subsequently tried, convicted and hanged. David Coleman Headley, one of the key conspirators who conducted reconnaissance of Mumbai before the attacks, later deposed before a court in India through video-conferencing from the US.Tahawwur Hussain Rana, another accused in the 26/11 conspiracy was extradited from the US in 2025 to face trial in India. Several masterminds and handlers of the attacks, however, continue to remain beyond India's reach with many believed to be based in Pakistan, PTI reported.The chargesheet filed in the case stated that the attacks were meticulously planned and executed after extensive training, preparation and briefing.Every year, floral tributes are paid at the Mumbai Police headquarters to personnel who lost their lives fighting the terrorists. Homage is also paid at CSMT, Cama and Albless Hospital and other locations targeted during the attacks.Mumbaikars also gather at Prerana Sthal, where a statue of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Ombale stands in tribute to the policeman who confronted Kasab with a lathi and was killed while helping capture the terrorist at Girgaon Chowpatty in south Mumbai.
Article Summary: Advocates Amin Solkar and Farhana Shah represented Ajmal Kasab before the Bombay high court for nine months. The two had set aside their other cases to defend the lone captured Pakistani terrorist. Both lawyers say their dues remain unpaid despite the high court proceedings having concluded more than a decade ago.

Article Title: Trump slaps new tariffs on 14 nations; India faces additional 17%
Article Text:
A 3D-printed miniature model of US President Donald Trump, the Indian flag and the word "Tariffs" appear in this illustration taken November 25, 2026.

Intense trade negotiations with US likely in coming weeks

Government rejects structural excess capacity charge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Setting the stage for additional duty burden on exports, the US Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed 17 per cent additional tariffs on Indian goods, which can rise to 25 per cent if the bilateral trade deal is not signed.Citing the findings of its Section 301 investigation against 16 countries for alleged structural excess capacity, the Trump administration has proposed additional levies of 15-20 per cent against 14 offending countries, with the developed nations at the lower end of the band and China, Vietnam and Singapore at the top. The move, though not surprising, creates fresh complications for exporters, with two important exports from India, pharma and mobile phones, exempted from additional tariffs.While most developing countries are in the 18 per cent bracket, India has a one-percentage-point “comparative advantage”, provided the first tranche of the agreement which was finalised last Feb, is signed by the time the final hearings are completed and tariffs are announced. With the hearings scheduled on Jan 25, 2027, the fresh levies are likely to kick in next Feb. In India’s case, the probe flagged PLI schemes as part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat push and sector-specific acts, policies and practices in the steel, solar, health and ICT sectors.The US Trade Representative (USTR) also cited the rise in imports from China — which government ironically has struggled to check for its own reasons — as an instance of failure to address imports and FDI from non-market economies.Going by USTR’s statement, the Section 301 probe faulted countries, some following economic models vastly different from others, for actions that almost every government takes to support domestic industry: plans and policies that expand manufacturing and exports, financial repression, market access barriers and failure to address global excess capacity including through imports and FDI from non-market economies like China.In the absence of a trade deal, additional tariffs can be imposed, setting the stage for intense negotiations in the coming weeks.Although fresh tariffs were expected, the announcement plunges the industry into fresh uncertainty as it negotiates contracts for the 2027 winter with exporters keen to ship goods before the new tariffs kick in.Exporters will be watching the next move from government.The first Section 301 action is already facing a legal challenge in the US, and the latest move too is likely to land in American courts.USTR’s move signals that Trump has not lost his appetite for tariffs as one of the favourite items on his policy menu despite higher inflation causing a setback in the midterm elections.USTR’s big grouse is India’s trade surplus, estimated at $57 billion in 2025, when the country had a global trade deficit of $309 billion.“In particular, India’s acts, policies, and practices: (1) create unfair competition and reduce commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters; (2) harm the US economy through loss of US domestic manufacturing and exports; and (3) increase US economic security risks, including through reliance on NME inputs,” it concluded.The government on Wednesday rejected charges of structural excess capacity in any sector, and said it will work with the US for early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement. “India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a BTA. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations,” government said, adding it was examining the USTR notice.While India and the US had announced an agreement on Feb 2, agreeing to 18 per cent additional tariff, it had to be suspended due to the reciprocal tariffs being struck down by the US Supreme Court.The government officials have said that the agreement has largely been finalised and will be sealed once the US tariff framework is ready.
Article Summary: The US Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed 17 per cent additional tariffs on Indian goods, which can rise to 25 per cent if the bilateral trade deal is not signed. The move creates fresh complications for exporters, with two important exports from India, pharma and mobile phones, exempted from additional tariffs.

Article Title: Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case
Article Text:
The non-compliance stood out against the backdrop of opposition to the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon from Sikandar Badusha Dargah Committee, state govt, its Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, the Madurai district administration, and the Temple Board of Trustees

Collector apologises for lamp not being lit atop Deepathoon

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu government’s failure to comply with the Supreme Court ’s order to allow the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop deepathoon as a one-time arrangement may lead to contempt proceedings.On Wednesday, the Supreme Court said it would hear the contempt case despite the Madurai Collector’s apology to the court. A fresh petition has also been filed seeking directions to light the lamp atop deepathoon, the disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.Appearing for the Collector, senior advocate Gopal Sankarnarayanan told a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi that the court’s order could not be carried out and the lamp was not lit at the assigned place. He also said the Collector had filed a report.The non-compliance stood out against the backdrop of opposition to the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon from Sikandar Badusha Dargah Committee, state government, its Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, the Madurai district administration, and the Temple Board of Trustees.An array of political parties TVK as well as its predecessor in office, DMK, Congress, Left parties and Muslim outfits, have been opposing the move.In a twist to the controversy, the temple administration’s explanation for retaining the customary lighting venue came under question after four sthanikars (traditional temple priests) said their communication regarding lighting the lamp near Uchi Pillaiyar temple was sent last year and that they had submitted no letter regarding this year’s festival. The trustees had cited the priests’ views as one of the reasons for their decision to light the lamp at the customary spot.Senior advocate Guru Krishna Kumar, appearing for the petitioner, told the SC bench there was a “deliberate attempt” not to comply with the apex court’s directive. Kumar again told the bench in the afternoon that a devotee had filed a fresh plea seeking a directive to light the deepam atop the disputed Deepathoon with the flame from the lamp lit Tuesday. The court said it would hear this plea too.Meanwhile, a litigant made a mention before Madras HC seeking to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings over non-compliance with SC’s directive.In the status report, the Madurai collector said he had made all efforts to comply with SC’s directive, and he should not be blamed for failure to do so. “I submit that I took all the steps to comply with the order in good faith....I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon.However, the board of trustees resolved to light the lamp at the customary place,” the report said.SC had allowed the lighting of the traditional lamp at Deepathoon on Nov 24 as a one-time measure and directed only authorised persons to attend the ceremony.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court said it would hear the contempt case despite the Madurai Collector’s apology to the court. A fresh petition has also been filed seeking directions to light the lamp atop deepathoon, the disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.

Article Title: ‘Fighting against BJP or us?’ Congress slams Samajwadi Party over its list
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had sought to ease tensions Tuesday, describing the 2027 polls as a “historic opportunity” for the allies to jointly take on BJP.

Want Akhilesh as CM, but won’t settle for less than 100 seats: Congress

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

LUCKNOW/DELHI/MEERUT: Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Wednesday whether Samajwadi Party intended to fight BJP or Congress after SP announced five candidates, including four sitting MLAs, while seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls were still under way, triggering a fresh flashpoint between the allies.SP had offered Congress 26 constituencies against its wish-list of 131 as seat-sharing negotiations stretched to 3.5 hours in New Delhi on Tuesday, considerably longer than Monday’s 15-minute opening round. Later at night, SP announced its list of five, putting the alliance under strain.Masood said Congress was SP’s ally, “not a beggar”, and warned that if it could announce candidates during negotiations, his party could do the same. “When you make such an announcement against me, I don’t understand whether you want to fight me, Congress, or BJP,” he said.Masood took exception to SP’s list, which included candidates from Behat and Saharanpur. Congress is said to have sought both these seats, with Masood representing Saharanpur in Lok Sabha.SP sought to contain the fallout, dismissing Masood’s remarks as personal and insisting the candidate announcement was not unilateral.Ghosi MP Rajiv Rai said the two parties had agreed that constituencies held by sitting MLAs would not be part of seat-sharing negotiations, while Sambhal MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq said SP had received no such objection from Congress as a party.“As far as the issue of Imran Masood Sahib’s displeasure is concerned, I believe that, for the time being, it is a personal matter. We have not received any such message from our party or Congress,” the Sambhal MP said.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had sought to ease tensions Tuesday, describing the 2027 polls as a “historic opportunity” for the allies to jointly take on BJP. He said seat-sharing should hinge on winnability rather than quotas and indicated the 26 seats offered to Congress so far were not the final tally.AICC in-charge for UP Rajendra Pal Gautam backed Masood’s objection, calling the announcement premature. “This was wrong. It should not have been done. As a responsible political party, they should have waited. The list could have been announced after the discussions concluded. There was no urgency.”Gautam said Congress’s MP for Saharanpur made it imperative for the constituency to be discussed before candidates were named. He nevertheless described the 3.5-hour negotiations as positive and reiterated Congress’s demand for a “respectable” share, saying the party would not settle for fewer than 100 of UP’s 403 seats. Congress wanted Akhilesh to become CM, but would not compromise on its workers’ dignity or organisational interests, he said.Congress Legislature Party functionary Virendra Chaudhary called SP’s announcement a “violation of gathbandhan dharma”, while UP Congress president Aradhana Misra declined to comment.The allies had won a combined 43 Lok Sabha seats in UP in 2024, with SP securing 37 and Congress six. But the assembly seat-sharing bargain has proved more difficult as Congress seeks to rebuild its organisation and SP protects its sitting MLAs and electoral strongholds.SP is set to unveil the first of its election manifestos Thursday, with youth, education, social justice, Dalit issues, agriculture, farmers, law and order, industry and MSMEs among the key themes. A separate manifesto focused on women is expected later.SP’s early candidate announcement also brought Kairana back into focus with the renomination of three-time MLA Nahid Hasan, who won the seat in 2022 while in jail following his arrest under the Gangsters Act. He defeated his nearest rival by nearly 25,000 votes and secured bail from Allahabad HC in Dec 2022. His sister Iqra Hasan won Kairana’s Lok Sabha seat in 2024, defeating BJP’s Pradeep Chaudhary by more than 69,000 votes.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood questioned whether Samajwadi Party intended to fight BJP or Congress. SP announced five candidates, including four sitting MLAs, while seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls were still under way. Masood said Congress was SP’s ally, “not a beggar” and warned that if it could announce candidates during negotiations, his party could do the same.

Allahabad high court to hear Rahul Gandhi’s plea against PIL: SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed an Allahabad HC order asking the CBI and ED to probe complaints about leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi ’s alleged disproportionate assets and directed the HC to conduct a fresh hearing on the petition with an opportunity for him to oppose it.The top court principally set aside the order because of its ex parte nature, holding that not being given an opportunity to counter the allegations made in the PIL by Karnataka-based BJP worker Shishir Vignesh breached principles of natural justice.While the Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed Allahabad high court’s order directing a probe into the assets of the leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, it did not consider Rahul Gandhi’s plea for transfer of the PIL to any other HC or the SC.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal said HC adopted a process “completely unknown to law” while passing the impugned order as it did not even seek Gandhi’s response and permitted a witch-hunt without questioning the petitioner’s locus standi.The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that HC, during the fresh hearing on Vignesh’s PIL, would hear Gandhi’s submissions against the petition, including the maintainability of such a petition before a constitutional court and the locus standi of the petitioner to raise such issues through a writ petition.On August 17, SC had barred CBI, ED or any other authority from filing any report before HC pursuant to its July 20 order and directed HC to defer the proceedings till further orders. For CBI, additional solicitor general S V Raju had told the court that CBI is only verifying the complaint and has not commenced a probe yet. “CBI has not registered even a preliminary enquiry. The complaint may be wrong or right on facts. If they are right, then it is a gross case of disproportionate assets,” he had said.CJI Kant had said, “In our understanding of the law, police or any probe agency, if they have prima facie material they can register a case, investigate it and can proceed against anyone. No permission is required from the accused. But what appears to us, subject to assistance from both sides, is that if the court wants to issue a direction, it is expected to follow principles of natural justice.”Gandhi, in his special leave petition, had said, “Since 2024, Shishir, who, it appears from public reporting, is a member of BJP — a party whose politics and ideology the Petitioner (Gandhi) and his party (Congress) vehemently contest — has instituted multiple proceedings before different forums, including successive PILs concerning the Petitioner’s alleged foreign citizenship and criminal proceedings seeking registration of an FIR. ..”

Supreme Court quashed an Allahabad HC order asking the CBI and ED to probe complaints about leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi ’s alleged disproportionate assets. The top court principally set aside the order because of its ex parte nature.

Article Title: A commitment to strengthen our Constitution
Article Text:
'For crores of Indians, including me, the Constitution of India is an inseparable part of our life journeys.'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The writer is the Prime Minister of India

On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted our Constitution. Today, we remember Dr Rajendra Prasad, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and every member of the Constituent Assembly. Their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution.For a nation as diverse as Bharat, with its numerous faiths, languages, customs and schools of thought, it is important that the Constitution has a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Our endeavour has been to deepen its connect with the collective consciousness of our people, especially our youth and strengthen the spirit of unity essential to India’s bright future. That is why over a decade ago, our government decided to mark November 26 as Constitution Day.For crores of Indians, including me, the Constitution of India is an inseparable part of our life journeys. Whenever I look back at my childhood, the humble circumstances in which I grew up, the struggles that were a part of everyday life, I am filled with an overwhelming sense of gratitude towards our Constitution. That a child born into a family of modest means, with no privileges or advantages of birth, could one day be entrusted with the responsibility of serving the world’s largest democracy speaks volumes about how extraordinary our Constitution is.It is due to our Constitution that circumstances of one’s birth no longer determine the limits of one’s future.In our own humble way, we have sought to repay this debt of gratitude by strengthening our Constitution.The distinguished constitutional scholar, Granville Austin, described our Constitution as “first and foremost a social document”. The quest for social and economic justice runs through the very fabric of our Constitution. Thus, what can be more satisfying than working towards the realisation of this cherished vision of the makers of our Constitution?A recent World Bank report highlights that nearly 50 crore Indians have moved out of poverty. Breaking free from generations of deprivation, crores of parents can now dream of a better future for their children.When PM Awas Yojana ensures a family moves from a thatched roof to a pucca home, the constitutional promise of dignity acquires meaning.When Ujjwala Yojana frees a mother from the hardships of a smoke-filled kitchen, we advance the ideals of equality and well-being.When Ayushman Bharat enables a poor family to access quality healthcare without the fear of debt, social justice becomes a lived reality.When MUDRA and PM-SVANidhi provide collateral-free credit to small entrepreneurs and street vendors, economic justice finds expression.When digital technology and platforms like UPI transcend all divides and place opportunities once available to a privileged few within the reach of every citizen, we advance the constitutional ideal of inclusivity.There are many more manifestations of this constitutional vision.The list of amendments we brought can be viewed through the same prism. The 101st Amendment ushered in GST, a long-awaited reform. The 102nd Amendment granted constitutional status to National Commission for Backward Classes, fulfilling a long-standing dream of the marginalised sections of society.The 103rd Amendment received broad social acceptance. By providing reservation to Economically Weaker Sections, it addressed the long-overlooked aspirations of economically disadvantaged families from communities outside the existing reservation framework.For the first time since 1950, an updated version of our Constitution is now available in all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule. This has brought our Constitution closer to the people.Even after our Constitution came into force in 1950, we continued to be governed by the colonial penal code dating back to the 1860s. With Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, we have sought to bring about a fundamental shift in our criminal justice system, moving from the colonial emphasis on punishment (Dand) to a citizen-centric pursuit of justice (Nyay).Over the past decade, we have laid special emphasis on Kartavya, or the duties of a citizen. Our civilisation has always emphasised the responsibilities that accompany every role in society. The spirit of Kartavya has found expression in several mass movements, from Swachh Bharat to water conservation and environmental protection.However, there is another reality that I feel compelled to share. There have been occasions in our history when those entrusted with upholding Constitution chose to weaken it. Ironically, they are the same people who had the opportunity to govern India for five decades.This year marks 75 years since the First Amendment of 1951, when a government that was not popularly elected used its majority in the Provisional Parliament to restrict fundamental freedoms. Its timing, barely months before India’s first general election, proves that it was intended to influence the electoral process and stifle public opposition. It is also 50 years since the 42nd Amendment at the height of Emergency. This curtailed judicial review and fundamentally altered the balance of institutional powers. I would also urge youngsters to study the 38th and 39th Amendments to know what a power-hungry and anti-constitutional leadership can do.The repeated misuse of Article 356 to dismiss elected state governments presents another troubling chapter. One party has the dubious record of imposing Article 356 almost a hundred times and one former PM has scored a half-century in this field.The makers of our Constitution had hoped that it would be implemented in letter and spirit across India. But, for over 70 years, Articles 370 and 35A did not allow the full Constitution to be implemented in Jammu & Kashmir, thus trampling over the rights of SC, ST, OBC communities and women. It was only in 2019 that this historical wrong was corrected.For decades, in several parts of India, particularly in tribal areas, Naxalites used the might of the gun to deny the poorest people the rights guaranteed to them by our Constitution. The successful elimination of Naxalism this year is particularly heartwarming because it has ensured that the poorest of the poor can finally exercise their constitutional rights without fear. Now, we are left only with ‘Dimagi Naxals’, far removed from the realities of our times but persistent in their efforts to derail our growth trajectory.It is most appalling that the biggest party in the opposition wants to reduce OBC reservation and bring Muslim reservations, something the makers of our Constitution, notably Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, were totally against.The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame. A legislation aimed at giving women adequate representation in legislative bodies was disallowed from being passed by the one opposition party, once again showing its disdain for constitutional values. I assure the Nari Shakti of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them.Our constitutional democracy has a clearly defined role for the opposition. Sadly, the leading opposition party seems to have become more of an Avrodh Paksh (obstructionist) than a Virodh Paksh (opposition). They should know that disrupting democratic processes is no substitute for discharging constitutional responsibilities.Today, India stands at a defining moment. As we work towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, two simple yet powerful principles can guide our collective endeavours: India First in our thinking and Kartavya (Duties) in our actions. With these as our guiding principles and Constitution as our source of strength, we can secure a bright future for generations to come.
Article Summary: On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted our Constitution. Today, we remember Dr Rajendra Prasad, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar. Their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat.

Article Title: PM Modi asks ministers to stay put & stay ready; next Parliament session likely before December 15: Report
Article Text:
PM Modi reportedly asked ministers to complete Parliament session preparations before December 15

Delimitation Bill likely to be a key test

Opposition questions delay, raises concerns over delimitation

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly asked his ministerial colleagues to complete preparations for the next session of Parliament before December 15 and avoid foreign travel in the run-up to it, signalling that the government wants ministers to remain available ahead of the sitting.The issue of the upcoming session figured at Wednesday's Cabinet meeting chaired by PM Modi, according to sources cited by news agency PTI.The prime minister suggested that the session be convened before December 15 and asked ministers to ensure that their respective ministries were ready.The Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs will take the final call on the commencement date and duration of the session, the sources said.The preparations come amid questions from opposition parties over the delay in convening the Winter Session. As of Wednesday night, the Monsoon Session remained unprorogued, more than 100 days after both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13.The absence of an announcement on the next sitting has also fuelled speculation about a possible special session, particularly in connection with the proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.With Parliament expected to meet before December 15, attention is on whether the government will bring the proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, linked to delimitation and women's reservation.The legislation failed to secure the required numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17. Its passage would require a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, amounting to 361 votes in the present 543-member House. With three vacancies, the House currently has 540 members.The ruling National Democratic Alliance NDA ) has 320 members and would need support from opposition parties to reach the threshold.The political arithmetic has changed since the Bill's defeat, with 26 MPs having moved out of the opposition camp. 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.Despite these developments, the government would still need additional support. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight, could play a significant role in the numbers game.The government is also learnt to be considering a formula under which Lok Sabha seats would be increased by 50% across states to address concerns, particularly among southern states, over the implications of delimitation.The proposed framework is understood to retain the existing inter-state share of seats based on the 1971 Census. However, no final decision has been taken.The delay in announcing the next parliamentary sitting has drawn criticism from the Congress, which has questioned the government's intentions and sought clarity on its plans for delimitation.Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the country should have been informed by now about the dates of either the Winter Session or a possible special sitting."What games are being played by the PM-HM jodi, assuming that the jodi is still together?" Ramesh asked, referring to PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.He also questioned the government's approach to securing the numbers for the proposed legislation and demanded details of its delimitation formula."By now having seen (through) the desperate efforts of the jodi to cobble together a super-tainted two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha, the nation is entitled to know what the PM-HM formula for delimitation is, assuming that there is indeed one," he said.Ramesh further alleged that the uncertainty surrounding Parliament and the Bill suggested that "there is something truly sinister that is being planned".Opposition parties are also expected to raise their objections to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar during the upcoming session.A ruling alliance MP told PTI that debate and voting on a Constitution amendment Bill would not be possible unless the House functioned in an orderly manner.The government faces procedural constraints as well: an extended sitting of the existing session requires at least two days' notice, while convening a fresh session requires a minimum notice of 14 days.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly asked ministers to complete preparations for the next session of Parliament before December 15. The preparations come amid questions from opposition parties over the delay in convening the Winter Session. As of Wednesday night, the Monsoon Session remained unprorogued, more than 100 days after both Houses were adjourned.

Article Title: 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice
Article Text:
Justice Rao has served as Chief Justice in 4 HCs over 3.5 years

Justice Rao served as Chief Justice in 4 HCs over 3.5 years
