NEW DELHI: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended as Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This would mark his seventh high court since his appointment as a judge of Andhra Pradesh HC on June 12, 2012.The collegium also recommended the transfer of Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bhakru to the much smaller Jharkhand HC, and the appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, a judge of Himachal Pradesh HC, as Chief Justice of Tripura HC. This will be consequent to the transfer of Justice Rao from Tripura HC to Karnataka HC.Justice Rao, after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, had opted for Telangana HC on Jan 1, 2019.Even when Justice M S Ramachandra Rao was a judge of Andhra Pradesh High Court, the collegium led by CJI T S Thakur had, in 2016 considered a proposal to transfer him out of his parent high court, but the move was stalled.A similar proposal was also stalled during the tenure of Justice Ranjan Gogoi as CJI.However, adverse reports about him forced the hand of the CJI N V Ramana-led collegium in 2021, and Justice Rao was transferred to Punjab and Haryana HC as a judge, where he served from Oct 12, 2021, to May 29, 2023. The collegium led by CJI D Y Chandrachud next appointed him Chief Justice of Himachal HC, where he served from May 30, 2023, till Sept 24, 2024.During his tenure there, the Supreme Court had quashed an HC collegium recommendation for appointment of judicial officers as HC judges on the grounds that he had proposed the names unilaterally without consulting his two most senior colleagues.The Justice Chandrachud-led collegium then transferred him from Himachal Pradesh High Court to Jharkhand HC as CJ, a position he held from Sept 24, 2024, to July 21, 2025.He was transferred by the CJI B R Gavai-led collegium to Tripura HC, where he has been serving as CJ since July 25 last year. If govt accepts the latest recommendation, Justice Rao will have served in seven HCs — and as CJ in four of them within a span of three and a half years.
Article Summary: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended as Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. Article Title: Saharanpur showdown: Why Akhilesh's 1st candidate list in UP has rattled Congress MP Imran Masood
Article Text:
Imran Masood has made back-to-back statements against SP as Akhilesh Yadav's party released the first candidate list.

The Saharanpur war

The Akhilesh-Masood equation

Elder brothers or stepbrothers?

The voter math

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav 's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list includes two constituencies that the Congress leader considers his political turf. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress in alliance negotiations, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.Released on Tuesday night, hours after another round of seat-sharing talks between the two parties in Delhi, the five-name list features four Muslim candidates from western Uttar Pradesh and an OBC nominee from Bundelkhand. The four Muslim candidates are sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha. Jyoti Lodhi has been named from Lalitpur.The move has particularly rattled Masood, who represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and is the Congress's Uttar Pradesh working president. Having won the Saharanpur parliamentary seat in 2024, Masood sees the two qssembly constituencies as important to Congress's claim to political space in the region. His sharp response has raised a pointed question: does the SP want to take on the BJP or its INDIA bloc ally?The SP renominated four sitting legislators: Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha.The fifth candidate, Jyoti Lodhi, has been named from Lalitpur.All four Muslim candidates are from western UP, where the SP is keen to retain its traditional support base and expand its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) coalition.But Behat and Saharanpur make the list particularly sensitive for Masood.The Congress MP won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in 2024 with 5,47,967 votes, defeating the BJP's Raghav Lakhanpal by 64,542 votes. He secured 44.57% of the vote, against the BJP candidate's 39.32%.His performance was particularly strong in the two assembly segments now at the centre of the dispute. Masood led by 44,626 votes in Saharanpur and 38,229 in Behat in the parliamentary election. Both, however, had elected SP MLAs in 2022.Umar Ali Khan won Behat with 1,34,513 votes, defeating the BJP's Naresh Saini by 37,880 votes. Ashu Malik secured Saharanpur with 1,07,007 votes, defeating the BJP's Jagpal Singh by 30,745 votes.The contrast is the main disagreement point between the allies. Congress is banking on the 2024 Lok Sabha mandate, while the SP is relying on its assembly-level victories and sitting legislators.For Akhilesh, the two seats are established SP territory. However, for Masood, they are part of the space where Congress can consolidate after his parliamentary victory.Masood and Malik were involved in a public exchange during a district development coordination and monitoring committee meeting earlier this year. After the SP announcement, Malik said he was under "no fear or pressure" and would contest the election strongly.Masood's nephew Hamza Masood was more combative. He asserted that Congress would contest all seven assembly seats in Saharanpur district, adding that his uncle's support was crucial in the region."BJP ko Saharanpur se Imran Masood hi hara sakte hain," he said.The latest confrontation is another turn in a political relationship that has changed parties, positions and equations more than once.Imran Masood left Congress and joined the SP in January 2022, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. But the association lasted barely nine months. After the SP did not give him or his associates a ticket, Masood quit the party in October 2022 and joined the BSP.Mayawati appointed him coordinator of the BSP's western Uttar Pradesh unit, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. That stint, too, ended abruptly. In August 2023, the BSP expelled him, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. Masood returned to Congress in October that year.The return proved electorally significant. In 2024, Congress fielded him from Saharanpur as part of the INDIA bloc arrangement, with SP support. He defeated the BJP, giving Congress a prominent Muslim face in western UP.But the parliamentary victory did not necessarily settle the question of who would control the political space in the region.The unease has been building for months. Congress's decision to appoint Masood as Uttar Pradesh working president in October was viewed by some SP leaders as an attempt to strengthen its bargaining position in seat-sharing negotiations. The Indian Express reported that sections of the SP were uncomfortable with Masood's public criticism of Akhilesh and his demands for an early alliance decision.In August, another development added to the strain. Imran Masood's son-in-law, Shayan Masood, joined the SP, citing ideological differences with his father-in-law. Shayan subsequently criticised Masood for targeting Akhilesh instead of the BJP.The candidate announcement has now brought the personal and political tensions into the open."When you make such an announcement against me, I don't understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress, or the BJP," Masood said, questioning the SP's seriousness about the alliance.He also rejected the idea that Congress was seeking charity from the SP. "We are not beggars," he said, objecting to the party's unilateral announcement of candidates while negotiations were still underway.The public sparring quickly drew reactions from both camps, with some leaders attempting damage control and others adding fuel to the fire.SP leader ST Hasan urged restraint, describing the two parties as elder and younger brothers."We are like elder and younger brothers. We should not talk like two stepbrothers fighting over division of property," he said.SP MP SP Singh Patel, however, was less conciliatory. He dismissed Congress's electoral strength in Uttar Pradesh and said the party would only be able to win by relying on the SP."The Congress should simply accept whatever number of seats they are allocated in the alliance," he said.Masood hit back, invoking Rahul Gandhi's role in Patel's political rise. He argued that Patel was an MP because of the political impact Rahul Gandhi had created after 2019.The exchange has exposed a fundamental disagreement over the alliance's power structure. Congress wants its improved Lok Sabha performance recognised; the SP believes its much larger Assembly-level organisation should determine the terms.Strip away the personal exchanges and the five-candidate announcement points to a larger contest over political representation in western Uttar Pradesh.The region has considerable electoral significance for both parties. Saharanpur district, according to Census 2011 data, had a Muslim population of 41.9% and a Scheduled Caste population of 22.1%. These are district-wide population figures, not constituency-level voter shares, but they underline the social context in which the two parties are positioning themselves.For the SP, the PDA formula is an attempt to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broader electoral coalition. Renominating four Muslim sitting MLAs in its first list reinforces the party's commitment to that strategy.Congress, meanwhile, sees its 2024 performance as an opportunity to rebuild its own Muslim-Dalit political base, particularly in western UP. Masood's Saharanpur victory gave the party a prominent regional leader around whom it can attempt to build that presence.The competition is not limited to the two INDIA bloc partners either. The Samajik Parivartan Morcha, a new alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), is another political formation seeking space among Muslim and Dalit voters.The BSP, too, remains part of the wider political equation, even as its organisational position has changed since the 2022 election.The SP has released a list of five, but the questions they have raised go well beyond Behat and Saharanpur. Who speaks for western UP's Muslim voters? How much space will Congress get within Akhilesh Yadav's PDA framework? And can two allies compete for the same electoral ground without undermining the alliance they are trying to build?For now, the SP has made its choices clear. Whether Congress accepts them, and whether the two parties can turn this confrontation into a workable seat-sharing arrangement, remains the bigger test.
Article Summary: Imran Masood has made back-to-back statements against SP as Akhilesh Yadav's party released the first candidate list. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.

NEW DELHI: A notice served to CJP activist Saurav Das on Monday evening by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to place of birth, had rendered his passport ineligible for foreign travel till the response was received and matter resolved.Sources in the govt said the mismatch in birth particulars across different set of documents like aadhaar, passport and birth certificate was flagged in inputs received over the last couple of months, prompting RPO to initiate a fresh verification of documents and information recorded in his passport application file. The passport was issued to him on Aug 21, 2019.While police verification is done either before or after issue of passport (in case of ‘tatkal’ passport), if any adverse or incorrect information comes to light during validity of the passport, a re-verification can be ordered by the RPO by issuing a show-cause notice to the citizen, asking why the passport should not be impounded.A notice was sent to Das by e-mail on Monday evening, asking him to respond within 7 days to the alleged “material suppression of facts” relating to his place of birth. He was asked to clarify the “incorrect” particulars with supporting documents, failing which he could face impounding of his passport under Section 10(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. The notice explicitly advised him not to use his passport till he had filed his response.“As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of,” an officer told TOI. “Das was well-aware that the pending RPO notice would be flagged in the immigration systems, preventing his clearance for boarding the flight to London. Yet, he chose to travel to the airport, possibly so he could play the victim after being stopped at immigration,” said the officer.Das, as per reports, however claims he did not see the email, which landed hours before his flight, till he checked his inbox at the immigration counter.A govt officer said Das has time till Nov 30 to respond to the RPO notice. “Let him satisfy the RPO as to which set of birth documents must be relied on. Once the RPO clears him in the re-verification exercise, he can resume international travel on the same passport,” said another officer.Sources explained that disparities were flagged only in the recent past in Das’s details like date of birth and father’s name across documents like aadhaar, passport and school certificate, issued from different places of his residence — Delhi and Puducherry.A PIL has also been filed in the Madras High Court relating to the alleged inconsistencies in his birth and parentage documents and even questioning his citizenship.
Article Summary: Saurav Das, chief spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), was served a show-cause notice by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai. The RPO asked him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to place of birth. A PIL has also been filed in the Madras High Court relating to the alleged inconsistencies.

Article Title: Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students
Article Text:
The gap between chemistry and business studies has more than doubled — from 2.9 lakh candidates in 2019 to 6.3 lakh in 2027 — an analysis of CBSE’s examination statistics registration data accessed by TOI shows.

Gap between chemistry and business studies more than doubled

NEW DELHI: The gap between science and commerce subjects in CBSE schools has widened considerably in eight years, with candidate numbers in chemistry growing by 70 per cent, physics by nearly 58 per cent and mathematics by 55 per cent, against around 32 per cent each in business studies and accountancy.As CBSE gears up for V Class 12 exams in 2027, with a record 19 lakh registrations, over half the candidates have individually opted for chemistry and physics. Chemistry has emerged as the most popular after English, with 10.8 lakh registrations, accounting for nearly 57 per cent of all candidates.Physics follows with 10 lakh (52.6 per cent) and mathematics with 8.3 lakh (43.4 per cent). English tops the list with 18.5 lakh registrations, accounting for over 97 per cent of the examination cohort. Economics, with 5.8 lakh registrations, has attracted nearly one in three candidates, followed by business studies (4.51 lakh) and accountancy (4.5 lakh), each accounting for nearly 24 per cent of the candidates.In 2019, chemistry and physics had around 6.4 lakh candidates each, mathematics 5.3 lakh and economics 4.3 lakh, while business studies and accountancy had around 3.4 lakh each. While commerce subjects continue to attract more students, their numbers have not kept pace with the growth recorded in core science subjects.The gap between chemistry and business studies has more than doubled — from 2.9 lakh candidates in 2019 to 6.3 lakh in 2027 — an analysis of CBSE’s examination statistics registration data accessed by TOI shows. The gap between physics and accountancy has similarly widened from 2.9 lakh to 5.5 lakh.The figures also reflect the steady expansion of CBSE’s examination cohort. Class XII registrations have increased by nearly 31 per cent in five years, from 14.5 lakh in 2022 to 16.9 lakh in 2023, 17 lakh in 2024 and 17.8 lakh in 2025. Registrations reached 18.6 lakh in 2026, with the provisional numbers for 2027 recording a further increase of 2.3 per cent.The dominance of science subjects in CBSE schools comes amid their growing popularity nationally. An education ministry analysis of school board exam results showed science accounted for 47 per cent of Class XII passouts across the country in 2024, up from 44 per cent in 2023. For the first time in at least a decade, more girls cleared Class XII in science than in arts in 2024.The board allows flexible subject combinations, and officials said the provisional registration numbers could change marginally.
Article Summary: Gap between chemistry and business studies more than doubled in eight years. Chemistry has emerged as the most popular after English, with 10.8 lakh registrations. English tops the list with 18.5 lakh registrations, accounting for over 97 per cent of the examination cohort.

Article Title: Anant Ambani’s Vantara signs 10-year wildlife conservation pact with Madagascar
Article Text:

Anant Ambani’s animal welfare and conservation organisation Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development to strengthen wildlife conservation and animal welfare efforts in the island nation.The non-exclusive Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed on November 24, 2026, recognises Vantara as Madagascar's conservation partner. The partnership will focus on returning Malagasy animals seized abroad, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, veterinary care, and rewilding, wherever possible.As part of the agreement, Vantara will support the development of Madagascar’s National Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre, expected to serve as a hub for conservation, research, and training. The facility will remain the property of the Republic of Madagascar and operate under the authority of its environment ministry.The collaboration will also focus on strengthening local expertise through training programmes, internships, specialist exchanges and applied research. Vantara may assist with health checks, disease screening, transportation, quarantine, and post-arrival care for animals being repatriated to Madagascar.The agreement comes amid growing concerns over the country's biodiversity. According to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, 90% of lemur species, which are endemic to Madagascar, are threatened with extinction, with nearly a third classified as Critically Endangered. The country has also faced challenges linked to illegal wildlife trade and habitat loss.Under the partnership, Vantara will provide scientific support, including field research and genetic profiling, to help determine whether rescued animals can be returned to the wild and to identify suitable release locations. The Government of Madagascar, guided by its CITES Scientific Authority.Madagascar's Environment and Sustainable Development Minister, Nolave Luck Aristide Andriatsihala, said international cooperation was essential to protecting the country's natural heritage.Vivaan Karani, CEO of Vantara, said strengthening the people and institutions responsible for wildlife conservation in animals' countries of origin would remain central to the organisation's conservation strategy.
Article Summary: Anant Ambani’s animal welfare and conservation organisation Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar. The partnership will focus on returning Malagasy animals seized abroad, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, veterinary care, and rewilding. The agreement comes amid growing concerns over the country's biodiversity.

The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the directorate of census operations to submit within a week the standard operating procedures (SOPs) governing the census, including the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information.The direction came after the Centre agreed to place the relevant SOPs on record before the court, news agency PTI reported.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant procedures.The bench asked her to provide the details within a week.The direction came in response to a plea by Aakash Goel raising concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying caste-related information under a notification issued on August 14 concerning the census.The petition sought disclosure of the methodology, applicable household schedule and instructions governing the recording and verification of caste particulars, while ensuring the confidentiality of individual information.The plea also sought a transparent mechanism to record identifying particulars of government-issued caste certificates, wherever available, and verify their authenticity through the competent authorities.The petitioner also sought a direction that caste data collected during Census 2027 should not be treated as the sole basis for formulating or revising reservation policies or determining caste-based allocation of welfare resources unless a transparent and verifiable verification protocol is put in place.It also pressed for authorities to submit an affidavit detailing the proposed protocol and steps taken to implement it.In an order dated October 12, the bench had asked the solicitor general to place on record the SOPs being followed for the census. Article Title: Hexagons for nutrients: Supreme court asks FSSAI to tighten front packet labelling
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) to use "total sugars" and "saturated fat", instead of "added sugar" and "added fat", as nutrients of concern in front-of-package nutrition labelling on packaged foods, alongside salt.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed the food regulator to ensure that each nutrient of concern is represented through a separate standardised hexagon carrying the corresponding pictogram and warning words, "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt", PTI reported."The FSSAI shall ensure that the FoPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern, each containing the words 'High Fat', 'High Sugar', 'High Salt', respectively, alongside their corresponding pictograms, rather than a single combined hexagon," the bench said.The court further asked the FSSAI to revisit and reformulate the threshold levels for each nutrient of concern.It also directed the regulator to ensure that sweetened beverages which do not exceed the prescribed nutrient thresholds are not displayed with front-of-package labels identical or deceptively similar to the warning labels prescribed for beverages exceeding those limits.On artificial preservatives and other additives, the bench directed the FSSAI to closely monitor product reformulation following the introduction of front-of-package nutrition labelling (FoPNL).The court noted that the FSSAI had stated in its affidavit that it proposed to adopt a single-phase approach to implementing the labelling regime. It directed the regulator to bring the regulations into force within its proposed timeline and take all necessary steps to ensure that it is strictly followed.FoPNL refers to nutritional information displayed graphically on food packaging to help consumers make informed purchasing decisions and choose healthier food options.The Supreme Court delivered its verdict on an application filed in a petition by public charitable trust 3S and Our Health Society, which sought directions to the Centre, states and Union territories to make front-of-package nutrition labelling mandatory on packaged foods.During an earlier hearing on September 28, the court had questioned the FSSAI over its proposed implementation timeline. The food regulator had told the court that it would need approximately four months to issue and finalise the draft regulations.It had also said the draft amendment regulations would be published for 60 days to invite comments from stakeholders through domestic consultation and the World Trade Organisation platform.The apex court had previously sought further clarity from the FSSAI on its proposed warning labels for nutrients of concern, including fat, sugar and salt.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to use "total sugars" and "saturated fat" as nutrients of concern in front-of-package nutrition labelling on packaged foods. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed the food regulator to ensure that each nutrient of concern is represented through a separate standardised hexagon.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Thursday questioned ally Samajwadi Party 's approach to seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying there was little meaning in holding alliance talks if SP went ahead and announced candidates before finalising the arrangement.His remarks came a day after the Akhilesh Yadav-led party announced five candidates while discussions over seat-sharing with the Congress were still under way."It is no alliance if one partner 'leaves' seats for the other after announcing its candidates," Masood said, questioning whether the two parties were being treated as equal partners. We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.Masood, who was part of the seat-sharing discussions, said the exercise made little sense if the SP was going to announce its candidates unilaterally.He declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, scheduled to be released later in the day, saying the functioning of an alliance should involve joint announcements and press conferences."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.The Congress MP from Saharanpur also recalled that his party had contested 107 seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, adding, "Now, he is yet to become the chief minister."Separately, Masood criticised the denial of permission for the Congress's Samvidhaan Raksha March, questioning the authorities' decision."What can I say? The Constitution that gives you power is the same Constitution that you want to trample upon," he said.Asked why permission was granted to a conference organised by AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi and Bhim Army chief Chandra Shekhar Azad, he said, "That is precisely the irony. This is the game, and people should understand it… People can draw their own conclusions."Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has continued to express his displeasure with INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing arrangements for poll-bound UP.Masood stepped up his criticism after the Akhilesh's party announced its first list of candidates.Questioning the SP's decision to offer the Congress only 26 "winnable" seats, Masood asked earlier, "Are we beggars?" and objected to the ally's "unilateral" approach to the negotiations.

Article Title: 'More obstructionist than opposition': PM Modi accuses Congress of weakening democracy on Constitution Day
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi offers his respect to the Constitution in the Parliament House complex, in New Delhi.

PM Modi cites amendments, Emergency and Article 356

‘Nari Shakti’ and Naxalism

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Congress on Constitution Day . He accused the party of weakening constitutional freedoms, misusing provisions such as Article 356 and obstructing women’s reservation, while describing it as an “Avrodh Paksh” (obstructionist) rather than a responsible opposition.In an opinion piece marking the adoption of the Constitution on November 26, 1949, PM Modi said the country’s constitutional journey had been shaped by both its founding principles and what he called repeated attempts by political leaders to undermine them.“Sadly, the leading Opposition party seems to have become more of an Avrodh Paksh than a Virodh Paksh,” he wrote, arguing that disrupting democratic processes was no substitute for fulfilling constitutional responsibilities.PM Modi also accused the Congress of attempting to reduce OBC reservation and introduce Muslim reservation, claiming that the Constituent Assembly, particularly Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, had opposed such a move.In the piece, PM Modi accused previous Congress governments of using constitutional powers to restrict freedoms and consolidate political authority.He said the First Amendment of 1951, passed by the Provisional Parliament before India’s first general election, had restricted fundamental freedoms and was intended to influence the electoral process and stifle public opposition.Referring to the 42nd Amendment, enacted during the Emergency, PM Modi said it curtailed judicial review and altered the balance of power among constitutional institutions. He also urged young people to study the 38th and 39th Amendments, which he said reflected the actions of “power-hungry and anti-constitutional leadership”.The Prime Minister further criticised the repeated use of Article 356 to dismiss elected state governments, saying one party had imposed it nearly 100 times and that one former prime minister had accounted for half of those instances.PM Modi also described the non-application of the full Constitution in Jammu and Kashmir for decades, due to Articles 370 and 35A, as a “historical wrong” that was corrected in 2019.PM Modi criticised the Opposition over the failure of legislation aimed at expanding women’s representation in legislatures, saying the episode should “fill our hearts with shame”.He assured women that his government would continue working to ensure their representation, adding that “no force” could prevent justice from being done to them.The Prime Minister also said the elimination of Naxalism this year had allowed the poorest people, particularly in tribal areas, to exercise their constitutional rights without fear. He added that the country was now left with “Dimagi Naxals”, whom he accused of trying to derail India’s growth.Concluding his message, PM Modi said India was at a defining moment as it worked towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.“India First in our thinking and Kartavya (Duties) in our actions,” he wrote, calling on citizens to make the Constitution their source of strength and work towards a brighter future.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi launches sharp attack on Congress on Constitution Day. Accuses party of weakening constitutional freedoms, misusing provisions and obstructing women’s reservation. Describes Opposition as an ‘Avrodh Paksh’ (obstructionist) rather than responsible opposition.
